name: Your morning coffee
headline: Beans from Vietnam and Brazil, energy to roast them, and a card machine to pay — three different chokepoint layers before you take a sip.
noticeWhen: Your café raises prices twice in a few months and blames 'shipping costs'.

dependsOn.via: Robusta from Vietnam and Indonesia reaches Europe through the Red Sea. When ships avoid it, the beans still arrive — later and dearer.
dependsOn.evidence: During the 2024 Red Sea diversions, Asia–Europe container rates rose sharply and arrival times lengthened by roughly two weeks.

dependsOn.via: The Red Sea route and Suez are the same journey — losing one means losing both.
dependsOn.evidence: Suez traffic fell by about half during the 2024 Houthi attacks.

dependsOn.via: The diversion route. Adds 10–14 days and considerable fuel cost to every sack of beans.
Vietnamese and Indonesian beans pass through here on the way west.
Commercial roasting is gas-intensive. European roasters price their gas off the same supply that heats homes.
dependsOn.evidence: European food processors passed through large energy-cost increases during the 2022 gas price spike.

dependsOn.via: The card reader on the counter. Most independent cafés have no realistic fallback if card authorisation stops.

name: A bar of chocolate
headline: Cocoa, palm oil and sugar arrive from three continents; the factory that combines them runs on imported gas.
noticeWhen: The bar stays the same price but quietly loses 15 grams.

dependsOn.via: Palm oil from Malaysia and Indonesia — a core fat in most mass-market chocolate — ships west through the strait.
The Asia–Europe leg for palm oil, packaging film and finished product moving to Asian markets.
Same corridor as Suez; closure pushes all of it around Africa.
Conching and tempering chocolate runs for hours at controlled heat. Energy is a visible line on a confectioner's cost sheet.

name: A loaf of bread
headline: Wheat through a single Turkish strait, fertiliser made from North Sea gas, and an oven that runs on the same gas.
noticeWhen: Bread, pasta and flour all move together on the shelf — that is the grain corridor, not your supermarket.

dependsOn.via: Russian and Ukrainian wheat — a large share of world exports — has one sea exit, and this is it.
dependsOn.evidence: Global wheat prices rose steeply in 2022 when Black Sea exports were interrupted, and eased when the grain corridor reopened.

dependsOn.via: Nitrogen fertiliser is made from natural gas. Gas price is fertiliser price is next season's yield.
dependsOn.evidence: Several European ammonia plants curtailed or halted production during the 2022 gas price spike.

dependsOn.via: Egypt is among the world's largest wheat importers and irrigates from the Nile. Pressure on either side pushes it harder into the world market.
Grain moving from the Black Sea to Asian and East African buyers transits here.

name: Fruit and veg in the supermarket
headline: Refrigerated containers, long ocean legs and diesel all the way to the shelf.
noticeWhen: Bananas and grapes are there but visibly older, and the price moved without explanation.

dependsOn.via: Latin American fruit reaches the US east coast, Europe and Asia through the canal. Reefer cargo cannot simply wait out a queue.
dependsOn.evidence: Drought-driven transit restrictions in 2023–24 cut daily crossings and pushed some traffic to longer routes.

dependsOn.via: Diesel for refrigerated containers, port handling and the lorry that completes the journey.
Counter-seasonal produce moving between hemispheres via the Mediterranean.
The fallback route — but ten extra days is a large fraction of a perishable cargo's life.

name: Filling up the car
headline: The most direct line on this map: one strait moves a fifth of the world's oil, and the forecourt reprices within days.
noticeWhen: Within 48 hours of a Gulf incident. This is the fastest-transmitting dependency in the atlas.

dependsOn.via: About 20 million barrels a day leave the Gulf through a 33km gap. No pipeline can replace that volume.
dependsOn.evidence: Tanker attacks in the strait in 2019 tripled war-risk insurance rates within days; explicit closure threats in 2011–12 and 2018 moved crude markets immediately.

dependsOn.via: Gulf crude and products bound for Europe exit the Red Sea here.
The same barrels heading east to China, Japan and Korea pass through here.
Products moving between Mediterranean and Red Sea refining centres.
Overland crude into central Europe — the alternative that gets stressed when sea routes tighten.

name: Buying a car
headline: A modern car carries over a thousand chips. In 2021 the world found out what happens when they stop arriving.
noticeWhen: Delivery quoted in months rather than weeks, and used prices rising above list.

dependsOn.via: Engine, braking, infotainment and driver-assistance controllers. Even basic models cannot be finished without them.
dependsOn.evidence: The 2021–22 semiconductor shortage left millions of vehicles unbuilt worldwide and drove used-car prices up sharply in the UK and US.

dependsOn.via: The ultra-pure quartz for the crucibles that silicon wafers are grown in comes overwhelmingly from one small area of North Carolina.
Permanent magnets in motors, sensors, speakers and electric power steering.
Every advanced chip in the car was patterned on a machine from one Dutch company.
Components and finished vehicles moving between Asian plants and European buyers.
Petrochemical feedstock for the plastics, foams and coatings that make up much of the interior.

name: An electric car
headline: Swaps an oil dependency for a minerals one — and concentrates it more tightly, not less.
noticeWhen: Lead times and battery-replacement quotes move well before sticker prices do.

dependsOn.via: Neodymium and dysprosium magnets sit at the heart of the traction motor. Processing capacity, not ore, is the bottleneck.
Cells and packs from Chinese and Korean plants ship west through here.
Battery management and power electronics depend on chips made on the far side of this strait.
Power semiconductors and controllers — more silicon per vehicle than a combustion car, not less.

name: Heating your home
headline: Four pipelines and one strait decide what a European winter costs.
noticeWhen: The standing charge and unit rate both move at the next billing period.

dependsOn.via: After 2022, Norwegian gas became Europe's single largest pipeline supply. The redundancy that used to exist no longer does.
dependsOn.evidence: European wholesale gas prices reached record highs in 2022 and household bills followed across the continent.

dependsOn.via: Qatari LNG is the swing supply that replaces missing pipeline gas — and it has one way out.
That way out is the Strait of Hormuz. Nearly a fifth of global LNG trade transits it.
Overland supply into central Europe, and a recurring instrument of political pressure.

name: The electricity bill
headline: Gas sets the marginal price in most European markets — and the renewables meant to replace it have their own chokepoints.
noticeWhen: Your tariff moves even though your usage did not.

dependsOn.via: Gas-fired generation usually sets the wholesale price at the margin, so gas moves the whole bill.
LNG fills the gap when pipeline supply falls short.
The exit for that LNG, and for the oil still burned for power in parts of Asia.
Direct-drive wind turbines use large rare-earth magnet assemblies. The green transition runs through Inner Mongolia.
High-purity quartz is used in the crucibles for solar-grade silicon as well as semiconductor wafers.
Japan, South Korea and Taiwan import almost all their fuel through this region. A disruption removes generating capacity for a third of world manufacturing.

name: A T-shirt
headline: Cotton and polyester from Asia, stitched in Asia, shipped west on the longest and most exposed trade lane there is.
noticeWhen: Ranges thin out and discounting stops before headline prices move.

dependsOn.via: The main artery between South and East Asian garment manufacturing and everywhere else.
The Asia–Europe leg. Fashion runs on tight seasonal calendars that do not absorb two extra weeks.
dependsOn.evidence: Several European retailers publicly flagged delivery delays during the 2024 Red Sea diversions.

dependsOn.via: Same route, southern end.
The long way round, and the reason a delayed season becomes a discounted one.
Polyester is a petrochemical product. Most of a fast-fashion wardrobe starts as oil.

name: Taking cash out of an ATM
headline: The most physical thing you do with money, and it still needs three institutional networks and a tank of diesel.
noticeWhen: 'Machine temporarily unavailable' at every branch in town on the same afternoon.

dependsOn.via: Two companies authorise the overwhelming majority of card transactions outside China. Your card is a claim on their network.
dependsOn.evidence: Both networks suspended Russian operations in 2022, instantly stranding domestically issued cards for international use.

dependsOn.via: Interbank settlement behind the withdrawal — the machine pays out before the money has actually moved.
The messaging layer banks use to instruct each other across borders.
Authorisation traffic is network traffic. It crosses the same cable landing points as everything else.
Cash is restocked by armoured van on a diesel schedule. Fuel rationing empties machines from the edges of the network inward.

name: Tapping your card
headline: Two companies, one clearing system, and a cable under the sea — between you and a sandwich.
noticeWhen: The terminal says 'cash only' and the queue behind you does not move.

dependsOn.via: Card networks are a genuine duopoly in most of the world. There is no meaningful substitute at the point of sale.
Dollar-denominated clearing behind cross-border transactions.
Cross-border instruction messaging between the banks involved.
For much of Asia, authorisation routes through this cable hub.
East African payment traffic depends on a small number of landings — as several countries discovered during 2024 cable faults.
dependsOn.evidence: Multiple simultaneous cable faults in 2024 disrupted connectivity and digital payments across parts of East and West Africa.

name: Your pension
headline: You almost certainly own assets settled through a Belgian institution you have never heard of.
noticeWhen: You would not — until the statement arrives. This is the least visible dependency here and one of the largest.

dependsOn.via: A central securities depository holding trillions in bonds and equities. Most European pension assets settle through it or its peer.
dependsOn.evidence: Roughly €190bn of immobilised Russian sovereign assets sat at Euroclear after the 2022 sanctions, demonstrating the settlement layer's leverage.

dependsOn.via: Cross-border instructions behind every international holding in the fund.
Dollar settlement for the US assets that dominate most global equity allocations.
Market data and trading connectivity between Europe, the Gulf and Asia land here.

name: Paying your staff
headline: For any organisation with people or suppliers abroad, payday depends on two networks with no alternative.
noticeWhen: International transfers sit 'pending' while domestic ones clear normally.

dependsOn.via: The messaging standard for cross-border payment instructions. Exclusion from it has been used deliberately as a sanction.
dependsOn.evidence: Selected Russian banks were disconnected from SWIFT in 2022, severely constraining their cross-border payments.

dependsOn.via: Nearly all large dollar payments clear through CHIPS and Fedwire. Dollar invoicing means dollar dependency even between two non-US parties.
Europe–Asia banking traffic crosses this corridor. Treasury systems fail over, but slowly.

name: Your phone
headline: The densest object on this map — eight chokepoints across four layers, most of them upstream of anything you can see.
noticeWhen: Launches slip, storage tiers vanish, and the 'budget' model quietly disappears from the range.

dependsOn.via: One company in Taiwan makes the overwhelming majority of the world's leading-edge processors.
One Dutch company makes every EUV lithography machine on earth. There is no second supplier.
The optics inside those machines come from a single German supplier. A chokepoint inside a chokepoint.
Two Japanese firms dominate the blank silicon wafers everything is built on.
The crucibles those wafers are grown in need quartz of a purity found in commercial quantity in essentially one place.
Nearly every phone processor licenses its instruction set from one company in Cambridge.
Magnets in the speaker and haptics; rare earths in the screen and camera.
Both the chips and the finished handsets cross this water.
Outside China and Apple's ecosystem, one company controls the operating system, the app store and the services layer that make a handset usable.
dependsOn.evidence: US restrictions cut Huawei off from Google Mobile Services in 2019; its international handset sales collapsed despite the hardware being unchanged.

name: A new laptop
headline: Same silicon chain as your phone, with a longer shipping tail and less room to absorb a shock.
noticeWhen: Configurations you want are 'out of stock' for months while last year's model stays available.

dependsOn.via: Processors and graphics silicon, including parts designed by companies that own no factories at all.
Upstream of every advanced part in the machine.
Wafer supply constrains how many chips can exist at all.
High-purity quartz for the crucibles those wafers are grown in.
Assembly in China and Vietnam reaches Europe and the Gulf through this strait.
The Asia–Europe leg for finished units.

name: Streaming a film
headline: Video feels weightless. It travels as light through a handful of cables you could count on your fingers.
noticeWhen: Quality drops to standard definition for a whole region at once, not just for you.

dependsOn.via: Where Europe, North Africa and Asia meet. A large share of intercontinental traffic lands at one Mediterranean city.
Most Europe–Asia cable capacity crosses a narrow Egyptian corridor. Cuts here have degraded service across two continents.
dependsOn.evidence: Cable damage in the Red Sea corridor in 2024 disrupted a significant share of Europe–Asia capacity and forced traffic onto longer routes.

dependsOn.via: The internet backbone for Southeast Asia converges here.
Nearly all cables serving East Asia funnel through one earthquake-prone corridor north of the Philippines.
dependsOn.evidence: The 2006 Hengchun earthquake severed multiple cables here and disrupted East Asian connectivity for weeks.

dependsOn.via: East Africa's connection to the rest of the internet rests on very few landings.
Encoding, recommendation and the AI features bolted onto every platform now run on one company's accelerators.

name: Your company's cloud and SaaS
headline: A software business with no warehouse, no fleet and no factory still sits on at least eight of these nodes.
noticeWhen: Latency to one region degrades, a provider declares a regional incident, and your SLA credits arrive a month later.

dependsOn.via: Europe–Asia traffic between your regions crosses this corridor whether your architecture diagram shows it or not.
A primary European landing point for intercontinental capacity.
Regional hub for APAC availability zones and the traffic between them.
The corridor serving Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese regions.
Accelerator supply now gates how fast any provider can add AI capacity — and what they charge for it.
Those accelerators, and the server CPUs beside them, are made in one place.
A disruption here is a simultaneous compute and energy shock for the entire region your infrastructure sits in.
Paying your overseas providers, and being paid by overseas customers.

name: A parcel you ordered online
headline: Next-day delivery is a promise about ocean freight schedules made six weeks earlier.
noticeWhen: Delivery estimates stretch from days to weeks across a whole category, not one seller.

dependsOn.via: The short route from Asian manufacturing to European warehouses. Losing it costs about two weeks per container.
dependsOn.evidence: The Ever Given grounding in 2021 blocked the canal for six days and held up an estimated $9.6bn of goods per day.

dependsOn.via: The southern approach. Avoiding it means avoiding Suez.
Almost everything leaving East Asia westbound starts here.
Asia to the US east coast, and the route that congests when the canal restricts transits.
Where the diverted traffic goes, and why freight rates move even for routes that were never affected.
The checkout itself.

name: Prescription medicines
headline: Most generic drugs in Europe and the US begin as active ingredients made in India and China.
noticeWhen: Your pharmacy substitutes a different brand, then tells you to try another branch.

dependsOn.via: Active pharmaceutical ingredients from Indian and Chinese producers move west through here.
The Asia–Europe leg for both ingredients and finished dosage forms.
Same corridor; temperature-controlled cargo tolerates delay poorly.
A large share of pharmaceutical precursors are petrochemical derivatives.

name: An MRI or CT scan
headline: Diagnostic imaging depends on rare-earth processing and advanced semiconductors — neither of which a health service can source domestically.
noticeWhen: Waiting lists lengthen for scans specifically, while consultations carry on as normal.

dependsOn.via: Rare-earth elements in magnet assemblies, detector materials and gadolinium contrast agents.
Image reconstruction and machine control run on advanced processors with long qualification cycles in medical devices.
Upstream of every one of those processors.
Machines and spare parts from Asian and European manufacturers reach their destinations by sea.
